reviews.title: Held for ransom
reviews.body:
The app works very well. The problem is that if you try to control your tv you’re bombarded with pop up ads for the premium version. Honestly if they’d just rolled a normal ad every 5 minutes or so it would be more bearable. 

It seems their strategy to get money is to hold your tv hostage until you pay them to have control of it.
If your remote breaks or you lose it and you need to turn off the TV until you can get a new one, this is a good choice. But at $45 for premium, you’re better off buying 5 replacement remotes at an average cost of $5-7 instead.
Not recommended.

Yesterday alone, I received 64 spam calls and texts in a single day. Today, I received another 44. That is completely unacceptable for an app I’m paying for specifically to stop this problem.

I block the numbers. I report them. I follow the recommended steps. Nothing works. My phone number is also registered on the “National Do Not Call Registry”, yet the volume of spam getting through RoboKiller has become unbelievable.

What is the point of paying for a spam blocking app when I’m receiving more than 100 spam calls and texts in 2 days?

RoboKiller used to work extremely well, which is why this is so disappointing. Something has clearly changed. Please fix the filtering technology and get this app back to what it used to be.

reviews.title: Not for journalists or other at-risk groups. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.body: If your wifi or mobile data connection is poor or drops, Nord will eventually stop trying to connect and simply disconnect entirely AND disable the Auto-Connect setting as well. When your wifi or data connection resumes, Nord will NOT re-enable Auto-Connect. It will simply remain OFF and your traffic will route without VPN connection protection. No warning. No notification. Nothing. You are on your own. You need to manually open the app to even realize that you’re unprotected, reconnect to a VPN location and finally manually re-enable the Auto-Connect setting. This is appalling. This leaves journalists and other at-risk users who rely on consistent VPN connections completely exposed. I just ran into this issue again (it has happened MANY times) because Nord - after years of knowing about this vulnerability - has done NOTHING about it. I’ve disabled auto-renew and will be switching to Mullvad or Proton after my term is over. I’m done.

reviews.title: Extremely disappointing experience
reviews.body:
I paid $49 for a one-year NordVPN subscription specifically because I was traveling internationally and wanted a reliable VPN. Unfortunately, it has been incredibly frustrating.

It worked occasionally, but most of the time it would just sit there trying to connect without actually connecting. When you’re traveling and relying on a VPN, the last thing you want is to waste your time constantly disconnecting, reconnecting, switching servers, and waiting for something you PAID for to work.

After dealing with this repeatedly, I contacted NordVPN support and asked for a refund because the service simply wasn’t working reliably for me. Their response? They refused to refund me.

So now I’m stuck having paid for an entire year of a service that I cannot reliably use.

I’m extremely disappointed. If a customer purchases a service and it doesn’t work properly for their needs, especially after trying to resolve the issue, I would expect the company to stand behind its product instead of simply saying they don’t provide a refund.

Based on my experience, I absolutely regret purchasing the one-year subscription. I paid for reliability and instead got constant connection problems and a refusal to refund my money.

Definitely not the experience I expected from a company as well-known as NordVPN.

reviews.title: Customer Support is beyond horrible
reviews.body:
UPDATE: I am still having issues. The VPN cannot resolve names because DNS resolving fails. Three weeks and their support people refuse to escalate this bug to their dev group. I am at wits end with them. How do you communicate with a brick? They won’t listen. All they do is apologize.

There are far far better VPN services out there. Ones which might actually care about their customers.

* * * *

I have been having issues for months which customer support is unable to deal with.

1. Their fast VPN reduced my network speed from 920Mbps to 180Mbps. After tweaking and many rounds with customer support, I finally manage 400-650. Better but nowhere near non-VPN speed. Their customer support agent even admitted to me customers can expect up to a 70% reduction in speed when the VPN is enabled.
2. You can specify a country/city combination to connect to but the software sometimes ignores this and connects to an entirely different combination.
3. This one is important: their domestic servers are managed by foreign ISPs. For example, a server in Los Angeles can be managed by/connected to an ISP located in the UK. I have experienced this first hand and it has caused me no end of trouble. I have been locked out of several of my accounts because the web sites thought I was logging in from outside my country.

Their customer support department uses a pool of agents. When they respond to your support emails you get someone different each time. They ask the same questions and tell you to try the same things. It's annoying to do things you know aren't going to work. I have reported several other minor issues months ago and none of them have been fixed.

What they don’t tell you is there’s a file size limitation, nor do they tell you the file size you needed. I just spent an hour trying to send a 30sec video. That never goes through, numerous ‘failed to send’ followed by ‘the file size is too larger’ prompts without it saying what is required. Most phones record about 100mb for 30sec at the lowest setting. I had to convert the file to 720p that file again to HEVC and still had to clip it down to 15sec just to get them to go through. Requiring a user to edit the lowest setting their phone can record and do a size conversion is not worth the extra money being charge to “send videos”.

reviews.title: Rip off when there are free alternatives
reviews.body:
Update after Dev Response:
There are alternatives that do everything your pro subscription model does for free.  They do it better, and they have more things available for a subscription model that is less than a quarter for what you charge - and they do it with zero ads!!!

No matter how you try to justify it, $9 a week - that’s around $30 a month (!?!) - is absolutely ridiculous when your app only does one small thing.  That’s not worth a subscription fee.  A one time payment, maybe?  But even then there are others who do it better.
Either way, it screams that you are trying to rip off those who are willing to fall for it.  That instantly made this product and company that no one should trust.

——————-

$9 a week for an app that should be a $5 one time payment for a basic tool.

It’s not worth it, and there are free alternatives that do even more available!!

At the end, they stressed this was a “one time” courtesy for what amounted to wasting an hour of my day for their data breach. Luckily my annual renewal was coming up and I was able to cancel my account without much lost. Zero chance I would use express as my VPN provider going forward.

Starting today 10/6/26 I CANNOT EVEN VIEW THE 20 SECOND CLIPS UNLESS I OAY FOR A SUBSCRIPTION?! You’ve got to be kidding me! Now all I get to see is a thumbnail unless I pay $7/month or $70/year per camera?! I was willing to overlook the short ads but at this point these cameras are useless and I’m replacing them asap and throwing them in the trash. 
**Original post**
When I first got these they were decent, never great but for the price I wasn’t complaining. Recently the cameras have decided to stop recording between 10-11pm every night (no sleep schedule setup on my end) and then resume recording around 5am all on their own. There is NO sleep schedule or downtime listed or assigned in my app but the cameras just stop recording on their own even when a few weeks ago I was getting motion alerts at 2/3/4am due to living on a thoroughfare. Also I’ve stopped getting notifications sent to my phone at all, yet the app shows multiple notifications on the notification bubble on it, which again I haven’t muted or turned off active notifications. When my subscription expires in a month I’m throwing these out and opting for something else because the delayed or no notifications isn’t worth it, and neither is the extreme lag time when you do get a notification but can’t immediately go to alive view. Save yourself the headache and money and get something else.

Obviously, this repeated malfunction represents a serious safety concern.

reviews.title: Simple and easy to use, but the App Store listing is misleading
reviews.body:
Find Air is a clean, straightforward device-tracker app that is easy to set up and understand. I can see the value it could provide in a one-off situation… especially when you simply need to identify whether a nearby Bluetooth device is present.

That said, the App Store screenshots create expectations the app does not currently meet. The images imply a map-based experience and more robust item-finding capabilities, but there is no actual map or navigation feature in the app. There is also no directional guidance comparable to Apple’s Find My experience, such as helping you walk toward a device with distance or directional prompts.
The app is also limited when the item’s Bluetooth Low Energy signal is unavailable because the device is asleep or BLE is disabled. In those situations, there does not appear to be a way to locate the device at all.

There is potential here, and the core experience is simple and approachable. However, the developer should either update the App Store images to more accurately reflect the current functionality or add the map, directional finding, and offline/sleep-state capabilities that users may reasonably expect from the listing.
reviews.author: Truth_Hurts_XO

translation.body:
寻找空气是一个简单易懂的 简单易懂的设备跟踪程序
我能看出它在一次性情况下能提供什么价值 特别是当你只需要确定 附近是否有蓝牙装置的时候
尽管如此, Appshore 屏幕截图带来了对应用程序目前未满足的期望。
这些图像意味着以地图为基础的经验和更强大的物品探测能力,但应用程序中没有实际的地图或导航功能。
也没有与苹果的“发现我”相类似的方向性指导,例如帮助你走近一个带有距离或方向性提示的设备。
当该物品的蓝牙低能量信号因该装置已沉睡或已禁用而不能使用时,该应用程序也受到限制。
在这些情况下,似乎根本没有找到该装置的方法。
这里有潜力,核心经验是简单和可接近的。
然而,开发商要么应更新App Store图像,以更准确地反映当前功能,要么应添加地图、方向发现以及用户从列表中合理预期的离线/睡眠状态能力。

reviews.title: Worthless app!
reviews.body:
This app doesn’t stop scammers that use virtual phone numbers. The user has to manually blocking each one, then the scammers just rotate to a dozen more virtual phone numbers and it becomes a neverending game of cat and mouse. The app is so stupid that it doesn’t recognize phone numbers with just a city or region in the caller ID field as being scam calls. There is no way to block all incoming calls that don’t have a proper name in the caller ID field. There is no way to block all incoming international calls (most of the scam calls I’ve seen are from Canadian and Filipino numbers). There is no way to make your phone white list only for incoming calls. This app is about a decade behind the times and is completely ineffectual. I am seriously considering my options in regard to switching phone service providers because of these glaring deficiencies in AT&T Active Armor and AT&T in general.

PS: To whoever the customer service rep is who is tasked with replying with 80% prewritten copy-paste replies: I will NOT email the user experience team or dev team about this, as I have already left my feedback here. Instead of creating extra friction and hurdles for users to go through, why not use some lean principles and simply forward the reviews to the user experience team and/or dev team? Otherwise, what is the point of what you are doing? It’s 2026. Nobody is really fooled by the “acknowledge, repeat user’s words, then move conversation to private channel” template response anymore. Just pass the feedback up the chain.

无法阻止所有在拨打身份识别栏上没有适当姓名的电话。

reviews.title: Don’t believe 5-star reviews.
reviews.body:
The app is misleading out of the gate—they coax you into writing a review for the app disguised as a required part of the initial set-up and they set the default rating to 5 stars.  Only then do they reveal that the app actually isn’t free, and is based on a subscription model, for which they are asking way too much for what this app actually is. 

Sad part is this could be a decent app with better transparency up front, and more reasonable pricing model.  

And yeah there’s a ‘free’ version with very limited functionality, but it is presented as if required to pay.  In short, the app is acting on bad-faith.

reviews.title: Slow and inconsistent
reviews.body:
I have a paid version of Proton VPN. It used to work great, but in the past 6 months the connections have been slow and unreliable. After 5-10 minutes of use, I too frequently need to change the connection. This is occurring on multiple devices. I submitted a ticket, and the fix was to install a third-party app that would allow me to use a beta version. I use the VPN for privacy so using an app that collects and sends data is not an appropriate recommendation. 

Please fix! I love the Proton package, but the current VPN is unusable.

10/13/26 update: I again emailed support since the reply to this post said that it didn’t look right that they wanted me to install third-party software. I uploaded my logs as requested, and the reply was to install third-party software. 

“Hello,
 
Thank you for the message.
 
This behavior should have been improved in our latest Proton VPN iOS Beta version, which you can download by following these steps: 
 
Download and install the TestFlight app……..”

I’m downgrading to one star for now and will post future updates.

reviews.title: Issues With Virtual Keyboard ⌨️
reviews.body:
Since the update to DuckDuckGo version 7.241.0, when I enter text into a webpage‘s search box, search suggestions appear, but are positioned behind/under the virtual keyboard. If I dismiss the keyboard using the confirm/done button, the page loses focus and the suggestions vanish. This issue did not exist prior to V 7.241.0, and the same webpages function correctly on other iOS browsers. Therefore, I’m forced to assume that the issue is with this latest update… 

iPhone 16 running iOS 27.0.1

reviews.title: Used to Work, but No Longer Shows USCIS Updates
reviews.body:
My I-485 has already been approved, and the approval is clearly visible in my official USCIS online account. However, this app still does not show the approval or any corresponding update.

What makes this more frustrating is that case status updates used to work correctly in this app for some time, but recently they stopped working reliably. So this does not appear to be a limitation that was always there.

If the app can no longer reliably retrieve certain USCIS case updates without requiring users to log in, that limitation should be clearly disclosed. Immigration cases contain extremely sensitive personal information, so I am not comfortable providing USCIS account credentials to a third-party app just to get accurate case status.

A case tracker should be able to reflect major public case-status changes such as an I-485 approval without requiring access to a user’s USCIS account. Right now, that makes the app much less useful at the exact moment when accurate tracking matters most.
reviews.author: Failed USCIS

我的I -485已经得到批准, 这一点在我的官方的USCIS在线账户中显而易见。

更令人沮丧的是,在这个应用程序中,用于正确工作的更新案件状况有一段时间,但最近它们停止了可靠的工作。
因此,这似乎并非始终存在的限制。
如果应用程序无法在不要求用户登录的情况下可靠地检索到某些USCIS案件更新,则应明确披露这一限制。
移民案件包含极为敏感的个人信息,因此我不太愿意向第三方应用程序提供美国独联体账户证书,以便获得准确的案件状况。
案件追踪器应能反映重大公共案件状况变化,如I-485批准,而无需查阅用户的USCIS账户。
现在,这让应用程序在准确追踪最关键的时候 用处小得多。

reviews.title: Not Microsoft Authenticator
reviews.body:
This app is extremely deceptive. It appears prominently when searching for Microsoft Authenticator and gives the impression that it is the official Microsoft app. After downloading it, I was immediately charged for a subscription.

The actual Microsoft Authenticator app is free, but this app seems designed to take advantage of people who are simply trying to secure their accounts. Users shouldn’t have to worry about accidentally signing up for a paid service when searching for a free, widely used authentication app.

I strongly recommend avoiding this app and making sure you’re downloading the official Microsoft Authenticator published by Microsoft Corporation. Apple should take a closer look at apps that create this kind of confusion.

实际的微软认证程序是免费的, 但这个程序似乎是为了利用那些 只是试图保护账户的人。
用户在寻找免费、广泛使用的认证应用程序时, 不必担心意外签约获取付费服务。
我强烈建议避免使用此应用程序, 确保您下载由微软公司出版的官方微软验证器。

reviews.title: This app is perfect for storing pokemon

The only complaint is how you can’t really do anything with the Pokemon in there, I don’t want anything too advanced but maybe a few Go-styled interactions would make it more charming. But the missions in there are a real pain when some of them specifically ask for a deposit from a certain game, and since Bank is shutting down soon some of the missions that require pokemon from DS games need to be CHANGED! You shouldn’t require a Pokemon from a SPECIFIC game just to get the sticker and decorations, the Pokemon in general is what should get the sticker instead. And also the trading is absolutely terrible. Everyone asks for the same Pokemon it turns one trade for one Pokemon into literal hours of finding a match.

reviews.title: Great potential but also great privacy concerns!
reviews.body: Love the device. Hardware is great. Works reliably. Problem is, software has a long way to go. It shows ALL of my upcoming reminders, even those I haven’t set through this device! You can’t turn it on or off according to a schedule or location…HUGE privacy concern if you have confidential meetings with clients. You won’t remember to turn it on or off manually. No way to select transcriptions in order to delete…even to select all. So the app is just filled with junk like TV shows or podcasts it hears. It is extremely useful as a reminder for things I speak of during the day, but the software should have been worked on before the device was released. It also bugs you EVERY TIME you begin to delete or save a reminder asking you why you are doing that. So many annoying things to it! Will be interesting to see if there’s another device that will replace this for me as there are many companies (like Plaud) that are looking at this space (BTW, I like Plaud too but I use it for different things).

reviews.title: Poorly Designed App
reviews.body:
My review is about the app, not the device. The device may be great and very useful, but the app is poorly designed.

For example, buttons and fields overlap recordings, making them difficult to access. If you only have a few recordings, you can’t scroll far enough to move them out from under those controls. Even the timestamps on the dashboard are cut off; the top row of pixels is missing from the text.

The app uses icons that look AI-generated, and the overall design has that same feel. There’s nothing wrong with using AI to code, but the execution needs work. It lacks the polish I expect from an app that pairs with a $130 product, and its features feel limited compared with other recording devices and apps I’ve tested. Their desktop app is better executed than the mobile app.

I also don’t see a way to organize recordings or summaries beyond a list sorted by date. There are no folders or tags that I can assign to conversations, only a search function. Even the date filter doesn’t seem to work correctly: selecting a different date changes the heading, but the recordings stay the same. For example, when I select yesterday’s date, the heading says “Yesterday,” but today’s recordings still appear at the top.

Speaker identification is inconsistent, too. In a conversation between two people, the app labeled four different speakers in the transcript, while the transcript summary said “detected 2 voices.” That contradiction makes it difficult to trust the speaker labels or follow who said what. This happened in every conversation I had transcribed.

One feature I really like is that the transcripts also identify background sounds, adding labels such as [keyboard clacking], [computer dings], and [toilet flushing]. It’s useful, but be aware that the app will try to identify the sounds it hears and include them in your transcript.

The free membership’s limits also need to be explained more clearly. Their marketing says you get AI-generated smart summaries, but the 150-minute allowance is labeled only as “transcription minutes.” What isn’t clear is that those summaries are subject to the same limit. I understand that a free plan comes with restrictions, but the wording should make it clear that once you’ve used your 150 transcription minutes, you also stop receiving AI-generated smart summaries.

If you’re trying to evaluate the device during the 14-day trial period, those 150 minutes can go quickly. You may need to pay for a month just to continue testing and decide whether the device is right for you.

I did really appreciate the shipping updates built into the app. My device took quite a while to ship, but I understood there was a large backlog while they waited for devices to arrive. Being able to see when mine was being packed, shipped, and delivered right inside the app was a nice touch. You can’t get past those opening screens until you receive your device, and those screens actually look polished. Unfortunately, that level of polish doesn’t carry through to the rest of the mobile app.

A UX/UI designer really needs to review this app. These are noticeable problems that make it frustrating to use.
reviews.author: kpence73

translation.body:
我的评论是关于应用程序, 不是设备。
设备可能很好,而且非常有用,但应用程序设计不善。
例如,按钮和字段重叠记录,因此难以访问。
如果你只有几张录音,
甚至仪表板上的时间戳也被切断; 文本中缺少顶行像素 。
应用程序使用看上去像 AI 生成的图标, 而总体设计也有同样的感觉。
使用 AI 代码没什么错,
与我测试过的其他录音设备和应用程序相比, 其功能有限。
他们的桌面应用程序比移动应用程序更好地执行 。
除了按日期分类的清单之外, 我也没有办法整理录音或摘要。
没有任何文件夹或标记可供我指定用于对话,只有搜索功能。
甚至日期过滤器也似乎不正确:选择不同的日期会改变标题,但记录保持不变。
例如,当我选择昨天的日期时,标题上写着“昨天”,但今天的录音仍然出现在顶层。
议长身份也不一致。
在两个人的谈话中,应用程序在笔录上标出了四个不同的发言者,而笔录摘要则说“发现两个声音 ” 。 这一矛盾使得很难相信发言者的标签或跟随谁说了些什么。
这发生在我所转录的每一段谈话中。
我真正喜欢的一个特征是,记录也识别了背景声音,增加了标签,如[键盘卡]、[计算机铃声]和[厕所冲洗]。
这很有用, 但请注意, 应用程序会尝试识别它听到的声音, 并将这些声音纳入您的笔录 。
自由会籍的限制也需要更清楚地解释。
他们的市场营销显示您得到了 AI 生成的智能摘要,但150分钟的备抵只被贴上“描述分钟 ” 的标签。 不清楚的是,这些摘要受到同样的限制。
我理解自由计划是有限制的, 但措辞应该清楚, 一旦你使用150个抄录分钟, 你也会停止接收 AI 生成的智能摘要。
如果你试图在14天试验期间评估该装置,
你可能需要支付一个月 只是为了继续测试 并决定该设备是否适合你。
我真的很感激 航运更新 嵌入应用程序。
我的装置花了相当长的时间来运送, 但我知道有一大堆的积压 当他们等待装置到达时。
能够看到当我的 包装,装运和交付 直接在应用程序内 是一个不错的触摸。
你无法通过这些打开的屏幕, 直到你收到你的设备, 而那些屏幕看起来确实被擦过。
不幸的是,这种水平的抛光并没有传到移动应用程序的其余部分。
UX/UI 设计师真的需要审查此应用程序 。
这些是令人瞩目的问题,使人感到沮丧。

reviews.title: The Favorites layout is the only thing stopping me from switching
reviews.body:
Brave is very close to becoming my default browser, but the Favorites layout on the New Tab page is the main thing stopping me.

Brave only shows 4 Favorites by default, even though there is a huge amount of empty space that could easily fit 6, 9, or even 12. If I tap “Show More,” it opens a separate Favorites screen with very large icons, so I have to scroll to find the site I want. That adds unnecessary taps and scrolling when the whole point of Favorites is quick, one-tap access.

Safari handles this much better. It shows 6 Favorites on the New Tab page by default, and tapping “Show All” simply expands the same page downward so more Favorites are immediately accessible.

Brave should use the available space better and show at least 6 Favorites on the New Tab page. “Show More” should expand the page downward instead of opening a separate, Favorites screen.

This is honestly the main thing keeping me from making Brave my default browser.

reviews.title: Beware of This App and Its Billing Practices
reviews.body:
I strongly recommend avoiding this app. I subscribed to Offender Locator but quickly discovered that someone I know is in the offender registry was missing from the results, which was extremely upsetting and made me question the accuracy of the service.

I attempted to cancel my subscription before being charged, but the app provided no way to do so. Every time I selected “Manage Subscription,” it claimed there was no subscription associated with my account.

I emailed customer support repeatedly requesting cancellation, but my requests were ignored, and I was charged $7.99 twice, even after explicitly asking them to stop billing me.

When they finally confirmed my subscription was canceled, they refused to refund either charge, despite the fact that I had requested cancellation before the charges occurred.

An app that makes it difficult to cancel, continues charging customers after cancellation requests, and then refuses refunds is unacceptable.

I have screenshots documenting everything. Save yourself the frustration and avoid this service.

reviews.title: Free trial is extremely difficult to cancel

I was then charged $7.99 anyway. After contacting support, they were suddenly able to locate and cancel the subscription, but refused to refund the $7.99 because the payment had “already been processed.”

I have screenshots showing the app saying it could not find my subscription, my Apple subscriptions showing it wasn’t listed, and the $7.99 charge.

A free trial should have a clear and functional way to cancel before being charged. Based on my experience, I strongly recommend avoiding the free trial.

reviews.title: BE VERY CAREFUL WITH THE 3-DAY FREE TRIAL
reviews.body:
I downloaded Offender Locator and signed up for the 3-day free trial. After deciding I didn’t want to continue, I tried to cancel before the trial ended.

The problem is that there is no straightforward way for me to cancel it.

The subscription does not appear under my Apple Account → Subscriptions, which is where I would normally manage a subscription started through an iPhone app. I also tried to cancel directly through the Offender Locator app, but instead I received an error telling me that I needed to contact their support team.

I did exactly that. I emailed their support team requesting cancellation, but I have received no response.

I also never received a confirmation or receipt clearly showing my subscription or explaining how it would be billed. That makes this especially concerning because I have no visible subscription in my Apple account and no working cancellation option in the app, yet the trial is apparently set up to convert into a paid subscription.

I genuinely don’t understand how I’m supposed to prevent a charge when the subscription isn’t listed with Apple, the cancellation option in the app doesn’t work, and customer support isn’t responding.

If you’re considering the 3-day free trial, please be aware of this issue and make sure you understand exactly who is billing you and how you can cancel before providing your payment information.

I’m leaving this review because I wish I had seen more warnings about this before signing up. I shouldn’t have to chase down customer support or worry about having to dispute a charge simply because I can’t find a functional way to cancel a free trial.

reviews.title: $10 PER WEEK?! This Feels Like a Rip-Off!
reviews.body:
This subscription pricing is absolutely outrageous. $10 per MONTH would already be excessive for an app like this — that’s $120 a year. For what, exactly? But charging almost $10 EVERY SINGLE WEEK? That’s over $500 a year for a tape measure app!

For that kind of money, I could buy a whole collection of high-quality professional measuring tools instead of paying for a questionable app.

I downloaded the app, realized it required payment, and believed I had deleted it. I NEVER used it. Yet I later discovered that I had been charged $10.58 EVERY WEEK without realizing the subscription was still active.

The charges appeared on my bank statements simply as “Apple,” making it difficult to identify where the money was going. I discovered these repeated charges almost by accident.

Six weekly charges totaling $63.48 — for an app I NEVER EVEN USED!

This feels like a deceptive subscription trap and, frankly, borders on a scam. I consider this pricing and billing practice completely unacceptable.

I requested a FULL REFUND of every charge, but APPLE REFUSED my request!

BEWARE! Check your subscriptions and bank statements carefully before this app quietly drains your money week after week.
reviews.author: Eugene BDS

translation.body:
这种订阅定价是绝对令人发指的。

但几乎每星期收费10美元?
一个磁带度量应用程序每年超过500美元!
为了这笔钱 我可以买一整套高品质的专业测量工具 而不是买一个可疑的应用程序
我下载了应用程序,意识到它需要付款, 并且相信我删除了它。
我从来没用过

我银行对账单上的收费只是“Apple”,因此很难确定钱流向何处。
我发现这些重复的指控 几乎是意外的。
六周收费共计63.48美元——我从未使用过的一个应用程序!
这感觉就像一个欺骗性的订阅陷阱 坦率地说,是骗局的边界
我认为这种定价和计费的做法是完全不能接受的。
我申请了全部费用,但请求取消!
鲍尔!
仔细检查你的订户和银行对账单 之前,这个应用程序 悄悄地耗尽你的钱 每周。

reviews.title: Decent, but Email Guard misses most scam emails
reviews.body:
I recently subscribed to a multi-device Premium Security plan.

After a first week of frustration in which Avast wasn't recognizing my Premium plan on iPhone or iPad, Avast fixed it after a call to customer support that got escalated to Tier 2 support.

The Avast feature I care most about is Scam Guardian using AI. To test the effectiveness of this feature, I connected Email Guard to an old account that receives lots of spam and scam emails. Email Guard has caught a few, but misses most, scam emails.

A telltale sign that an email is fraudulent is that it fails SPF, DKIM, or DMARC. Even after failing one of these obvious authentication protocols, Email Guard and Mail Shield usually can't tell that an email is fraudulent.

If Email Guard and Mail Shield aren't checking the widely-used SPF, DKIM, and DMARC authentication protocols for email, then Call Guard probably isn't checking the USA-mandatory STIR/SHAKEN authentication protocol for phones calls.

Checking SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and STIR/SHAKEN is the easy stuff that any scam-detection software should be doing.

I have a 1-year subscription to Avast Premium Security, but if Scam Guardian doesn't greatly improve its effectiveness then I probably won't renew my subscription.
reviews.author: JP_58305-1

translation.body:
我最近加入了一个多设备保障计划
在Avast没有认识到我的iPhone或iPad的Premium计划的第一周的挫折之后,Avast在向客户求助后把它固定了起来。
我最关心的是使用人工智能的Scam守护者。
为了测试这个功能的有效性, 我将电子邮件保护与一个旧账户连接起来, 该账户接收了大量垃圾邮件和骗取邮件 。
邮箱警卫接获了几封邮件,但最怀念的是诈骗邮件。
电子邮件是欺诈的信号是 它失败了SPF、DKIM或DMARC
即使这些明显的认证协议之一失败后, 电子邮件卫士和邮件盾通常无法辨别电子邮件是欺诈的。
如果电子邮件卫士和邮件盾牌没有检查广泛使用的 SPF、 DKIM 和 DMARC 认证协议的电子邮件, 那么呼叫卫士可能没有检查美国强制的 STIR/SHAKEN 认证协议的电话通话。
检查SPF、DKIM、DMARC和STIR/SHAKEN是任何诈骗检测软件应该做的容易的事情。
我订了一年的Avast premium安全, 但如果 Scam Guardian 没有大大提高它的效力, 那我可能不会续订我的订阅。

reviews.title: Not worth it
reviews.body: I think Incogni does actually do what they say; however, by submitted these requests for removal you are inherently proving to data companies that you are a real user. This in turn means that any of the brokers that “resist” Incogni’s requests for data removal can now sell your data for more money because it has been confirmed to be real. This is why it seems like you receive more spam calls and emails after signing up for the service. It isn’t Incogni selling your data, but it is them revealing that you’re a real person, which makes you a bigger target for people purchasing data.

reviews.title: Looks pretty - Removed features.  No warning, no thanks!
reviews.body: I’ve had this since it was Lookout Life (Since 2012) and paid for and carried Premium for all this time.  14 years.  Then Kiren is forced upon us and guess what?  NO Identity Theft Protection.  It was silently removed while their description of the “upgrade” says it monitors the same things when you pay for “Plus” but there is zero identity theft included.  I’m OUT.  This went from a plain looking AAA protection (On iOS and Android) to AAA looking D-list protection.  This “Upgrade” has given me absolutely zero reasons to keep it.  I can move over to Nord, get the same stuff with an actual VPN AND $1M identity theft insurance. You know, the service silently discontinued.   What a slap in the face to long time customers. We shouldn’t care what the pretty interface looks like. In fact, if we’re in it, we’re looking into a breach or problem, otherwise there’s no reason to open it past the setup!  Form over function is not the best for a security app. Since you’re priorities are to make a pretty looking app without disclosing discontinued services, I can’t trust you.  How can I trust a security company with my data when they don’t even disclosed the removal of one major feature?  I can’t.  Literally went from “I’ve recommended this to everyone I know” to massive texts to the same people telling them the one feature that made this stand out was silently removed. What a shame.

reviews.title: WHAT is happening to this app?!☹️
reviews.body:
I’ve been a longtime user and supporter of this app. Once upon a time, it was EASILY five stars! It made hosting and joining international Pokémon GO raids quick, convenient, and genuinely enjoyable. But these days? Not so much. 😒

1. HOSTING RAIDS IS PRACTICALLY IMPOSSIBLE!

I can’t get a SINGLE person to join my hosted raids anymore. Not one.
    Are certain accounts being prioritized? Are free users being pushed to the bottom of the list, or is there a bug preventing our raids from appearing altogether?
    I don’t know. But I DO know that hosting has become completely useless for me.
    I’ve already contacted support. The issue was acknowledged, but never actually resolved. As someone who’s supported this app for years, that’s incredibly disappointing.

2. THE PRICE$:

What the heck am I paying for if half the app’s functionality doesn’t even work?!! At a whopping $15 a month- Thats $180 A YEAR!!! And FOR WHAT?! An app that can’t reliably perform one of its most basic functions?!

Respectfully, YALL HAVE LOVIN’ YOUR EVER LOVIN’ MINDS 🤨

😩😩😩 so PLEASE , if someone could figure out why nobody can join my raids, I’d REALLY appreciate it. Because all things aside, I actually like this app… And I would love to see it returned to its former 5 star glory.
